title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.75: Hardness of Komlós

problems.sourceStatement: Can we prove some hardness statement about finding a coloring achieving Komlos guarantee or the Banaszczyk discrepancy guarantee?
problems.problem: Prove a computational-hardness statement for the task of finding a coloring that achieves the Komlós guarantee ($\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty = O(1)$, or the best known $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d,n\}})$ / Banaszczyk guarantee) for vectors in the Euclidean unit ball.
problems.wordDescription: For the general discrepancy-minimization problem on set systems, strong hardness is known: Charikar-Newman-Nikolov proved it is NP-hard to distinguish systems with discrepancy 0 from systems with discrepancy $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$, so no polynomial-time algorithm can find colorings of discrepancy $o(\sqrt{n})$ even when near-perfect colorings exist; Austrin-Guruswami-Håstad proved it is NP-hard to approximate hereditary discrepancy within a factor of 2. However, these results concern the optimization version (approximating the discrepancy value / worst-case instances). The structured promise problem here — given unit-norm vectors, find signs achieving the (guaranteed) $O(\sqrt{\log \min\{d,n\}})$ Banaszczyk bound — is not known to be hard, and no hardness result for it has been published. The question is whether such a hardness statement exists (or whether the task is always easy in a formal sense).
problems.mathematicalConditions: Setting. Input: $v_1, \dots, v_n \in \mathbb{Q}^d$ with $\|v_i\|_2 \leq 1$. Let $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) = \min_{\epsilon \in \{-1,1\}^n}\|\sum_i \epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty$ and $\mathrm{herdisc}_\infty(v) = \max_{J \subseteq [n]} \mathrm{disc}_\infty(v_J)$; let $K(d,n)$ be as in Problem 1.05, so $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) \leq K(d, n) = \widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ for every input. Problem (as posed). Determine the computational complexity of the Komlós problem: (a) given $v$, is it NP-hard to compute or approximate $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v)$, and within which factor? (b) In particular, is it NP-hard to distinguish inputs with $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) = O(1)$ from inputs with $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) \geq c\,K(d,n)$ for a constant $c > 0$? (c) The same for hereditary discrepancy, where a polylogarithmic approximation exists via the $\gamma_2$ norm (Nikolov-Talwar; Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar). Benchmarks. Charikar-Newman-Nikolov (2011): it is NP-hard to distinguish set systems ($n$ sets on $n$ elements) with discrepancy $0$ from those with discrepancy $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$; hence discrepancy is NP-hard to approximate within any factor in the Spencer setting (this does not transfer directly to the Komlós normalization, where every input has discrepancy $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ and the question is about distinguishing $O(1)$ from that bound). Austrin-Guruswami-Håstad (2014/17): it is NP-hard to distinguish set systems that admit a perfectly balanced coloring (discrepancy $\leq 1$) from those in which every coloring has a monochromatic set; in particular hereditary discrepancy is NP-hard to approximate within a factor $2 - \epsilon$ (as cited by Nikolov-Talwar). Nikolov-Talwar (2015) and Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar: hereditary discrepancy can be approximated in polynomial time within $O(\log^{3/2} m)$ via the $\gamma_2$ norm, so no super-polylogarithmic hardness is possible for $\mathrm{herdisc}$. On the algorithmic side, Bansal-Jiang (2025) find colorings with $\|\sum\epsilon_i v_i\|_\infty = \widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ in polynomial time. Complete resolution. Either (A) an NP-hardness (or hardness under a standard assumption such as the Unique Games Conjecture or ETH) result for distinguishing $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) \leq C$ from $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) \geq c\,f(d,n)$ where $f$ is the best existential upper bound at the time (currently $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$), showing the algorithmic question is as hard as it can be; or (B) a polynomial-time algorithm that approximates $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v)$ within a constant factor, or that finds an $O(1)$-discrepancy coloring whenever one exists. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) NP-hardness of distinguishing $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) \leq C$ from $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v) \geq g(n)$ for any function $g(n) \to \infty$ (in the Komlós normalization $\|v_i\|_2 \leq 1$); (ii) a polynomial-time algorithm approximating $\mathrm{disc}_\infty(v)$ within a factor $O(\mathrm{polylog}(n))$ in the Komlós setting, or approximating $\mathrm{herdisc}$ within a factor $O(\log^{\gamma} m)$ for some $\gamma < 3/2$; (iii) a hardness result for hereditary discrepancy beyond factor $2$, e.g. $\omega(1)$-factor hardness under NP $\neq$ P or a standard conjecture, or a proof that the $\gamma_2$-based algorithm is optimal up to constants under such an assumption; (iv) resolving the analogous questions for the Beck-Fiala normalization (columns in $\{0,1\}^m$ with at most $t$ ones), e.g. NP-hardness of distinguishing $\mathrm{disc} \leq C$ from $\mathrm{disc} \geq c\sqrt{t}$.

literature.title: M. Charikar, A. Newman, A. Nikolov, Tight hardness results for minimizing discrepancy, SODA 2011
literature.description: Proves that it is NP-hard to distinguish set systems of discrepancy $0$ from those of discrepancy $\Omega(\sqrt{n})$ (for $n$ sets on $n$ elements), so Spencer's bound cannot be improved algorithmically in the worst case and discrepancy is hard to approximate within any factor.

literature.title: P. Austrin, V. Guruswami, J. Håstad, $(2+\epsilon)$-SAT is NP-hard, FOCS 2014; SIAM Journal on Computing 46(5):1554-1573, 2017 (ECCC TR13-159)
literature.description: Among its consequences: given a $(2k+1)$-uniform hypergraph admitting a perfectly balanced 2-coloring (discrepancy $1$), it is NP-hard to find a 2-coloring with no monochromatic edge; this yields the factor-$(2-\epsilon)$ hardness of approximating hereditary discrepancy cited in the discrepancy literature.

literature.title: A. Nikolov, K. Talwar, Approximating hereditary discrepancy via small width ellipsoids, SODA 2015; arXiv:1311.6204
literature.description: Polynomial-time $O(\log^{3/2} m)$-approximation of hereditary discrepancy via the $\gamma_2$ norm / small-width ellipsoids, complementing the hardness results.

literature.title: J. Matoušek, A. Nikolov, K. Talwar, Factorization norms and hereditary discrepancy, International Mathematics Research Notices 2020(3):751-780 (arXiv 2014)
literature.description: Shows that hereditary discrepancy is characterized up to logarithmic factors by the factorization norm $\gamma_2$, giving a polynomial-time polylogarithmic approximation and hence ruling out super-polylogarithmic hardness for hereditary discrepancy.

literature.title: V. Bhattiprolu, V. Guruswami, E. Lee, Approximate hypergraph coloring under low-discrepancy and related promises, APPROX/RANDOM 2015; arXiv:1506.06444
literature.description: Hardness and algorithms for coloring hypergraphs under low-discrepancy promises, refining the Austrin-Guruswami-Håstad picture for promise discrepancy problems.

literature.title: N. Bansal, H. Jiang, Decoupling via affine spectral-independence: Beck-Fiala and Komlós bounds beyond Banaszczyk, arXiv:2508.03961, 2025
literature.description: Gives an algorithmic $\widetilde{O}(\log^{1/4} n)$ bound for the Komlós problem, the first improvement over Banaszczyk's $O(\sqrt{\log n})$, and proves the Beck-Fiala conjecture (discrepancy $O(\sqrt{k})$) for all degrees $k \geq \log^2 n$, together with an $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{\log n})$ bound for every $k$.

problems.verificationNotes: Re-verified on 2026-09-20 against http://aimpl.org/hereddiscrep/1/, the DOI records of Charikar-Newman-Nikolov and Austrin-Guruswami-Håstad, and the arXiv abstracts of Nikolov-Talwar and Matoušek-Nikolov-Talwar. On 2026-09-20 Google Scholar search links were replaced by DOI/arXiv links and the Austrin-Guruswami-Håstad citation was corrected to the paper '$(2+\epsilon)$-SAT is NP-hard' (ECCC TR13-159 / FOCS 2014 / SICOMP 2017), which is the source of the hereditary-discrepancy hardness statement. The factor-$(2-\epsilon)$ formulation is as cited by Nikolov-Talwar; the AimPL page itself states the problem informally.
problems.statusDetails: Open. No hardness result for finding a coloring achieving the Komlós/Banaszczyk guarantee is known; the closest results are hardness for the general discrepancy-minimization problem (Charikar-Newman-Nikolov 2011) and factor-2 hardness for approximating hereditary discrepancy (Austrin-Guruswami-Håstad 2013).
